audit.whatIsWrong: The level chart gives Urgot all seven stages, but whys[6] — the row that renders under the last cell — ends '… that cell is skill, not a free Kass win'.
audit.why: The chart and its own explanatory row contradict each other on the same card. The row is the considered judgement (it argues both sides: you assassinate his squishies with ramped Riftwalk, but his frame and execute win the straight duel), so the cell should read Skill and the rating should be the site's neutral 5/10. I changed win[6] and phases[6].side together so the two layers cannot end up disagreeing, and left the other six stages to Urgot — 44.44% over 9 games gives me no basis to move anything else.
audit.corrected: Two+ items is Skill at 5/10: you win the teamfight, he wins the sidelane duel.

audit.whatIsWrong: Disdain is named as the thing your whole pattern schedules around, in seven separate strings, and its cooldown and range appear nowhere.
audit.why: Disdain is 16/15.5/15/14.5/14 seconds at 475 range. Both numbers change how you play the lane. 475 is short — shorter than Null Sphere's 650 — so 'walk reachable with Disdain up' has an actual distance attached to it, and 16 seconds at rank 1 is long enough that a whiffed charge really is a window rather than a figure of speech.
audit.corrected: Disdain: 16s at rank 1, 475 range. It is shorter than your own Null Sphere — hold that gap and he cannot open.

audit.whatIsWrong: Disdain is described purely as a flip. The page never says it shields him, and never says it stops on the first champion it touches.
audit.why: Riot's text: 'Urgot charges in a direction, shielding himself and trampling non-champion enemies. If he catches an enemy champion, he will stop and hurl them out of his way.' Two consequences the page misses. The shield means the burst you land immediately after the flip is landing into a fresh shield, which is exactly the moment the current text tells you to trade back. And because it stops on the first champion, minions do not block it but a body does — relevant every time you stand behind a teammate near a choke.
audit.corrected: Disdain shields Urgot as he charges and stops on the first champion it catches. Do not trade back into the flip — the shield is freshest right then.

audit.whatIsWrong: Purge is described as generic grinding damage. Nothing says it auto-prioritises you once he has landed another ability on you, and nothing says it slows him.
audit.why: Riot's text: 'Urgot slows himself while he unloads his weapon on nearby enemies. Prioritizes enemy champions Urgot has recently struck with other abilities and triggers Echoing Flames.' This is the actual combo rule of the matchup — Corrosive Charge or Disdain does not just chip you, it marks you as Purge's target, so the two land as one package and there is no 'dodge the follow-up' once the first one connects. The self-slow is the other half: while Purge runs he is slowed, which is precisely when a 500-range blink walks away clean. Also worth knowing that Purge is 12/9/6/3/0 seconds and free at rank 5 — by the time he maxes it there is no cooldown window to wait out.
audit.corrected: Landing Corrosive Charge or Disdain makes Purge lock onto you. Purge also slows Urgot while it runs, so that is your Riftwalk window — and at rank 5 it costs nothing and has no cooldown.

audit.whatIsWrong: Fear Beyond Death is called an execute with no range and no cooldown, and the page never says it impales only the FIRST champion hit.
audit.why: It is 100/85/70 seconds at 2500 range and 'impales the first enemy champion hit'. The range is the thing: 2500 units is far outside anything else in this lane, so 'never blink into R range' understates it — you are inside R range while you are still farming. And because it takes the first champion in the line, a teammate standing between you and Urgot eats the drill, which is a real teamfight instruction for a champion whose job is to dive past the frontline.
audit.corrected: Fear Beyond Death: 100s at rank 1, 2500 range, and it impales the FIRST champion in its path — position behind a body, not beside one.

audit.whatIsWrong: breakdown.late tells you to 'Q-silence the counterplay'.
audit.why: Null Sphere has never silenced in this kit version — Riot's text is 'dealing damage and interrupting channels' plus a magic-absorbing shield. Against Urgot specifically the interrupt has nothing to catch either, since no ability in his kit carries a channel flag, so the honest version of this line is the shield and the blink, not a lockout.
audit.corrected: Null Sphere interrupts channels; it does not silence.

audit.why: Corrosive Charge carries a 'dash' derived flag in the kit file, which contradicts Riot's own description ('Fires an explosive charge at the target location'). Treated as a tooltip-parsing misfire and NOT written into the page as a second gap-closer. The page is already right to name Disdain as his only engage.
44.44% over 9 games. The page quotes no figure and I did not use this sample to justify any prose change.

edits.before: Still his lane. By levels 4-5 you can recover some mana with Nether Blade and farm under tower, but one mistimed step-up gets you hit by E Disdain and ground down by W before you react. Six changes things slightly: Riftwalk is your first real tool — it lets you blink out of his E flip and disengage, so spend it dodging his all-in and ganks, not all-inning him. Never blink toward him: if you Riftwalk into his range while he can land R, the execute finishes you and the fear locks the kill.
edits.after: Still his lane. By levels 4-5 you can recover mana with Nether Blade and farm under tower, but one mistimed step-up eats Disdain (16s at rank 1) and then Purge, which locks onto whoever he last hit with an ability. Six changes things: Riftwalk is your first real tool — blink the instant he commits the charge, and remember Purge slows him while it runs. Never blink toward him: Fear Beyond Death reaches 2500 units, and low HP inside that line is the execute.

edits.before: Riftwalk finally gives you an answer to his E Disdain flip — blink out the moment he commits the charge, dodge the W follow-up, and reset; it's your one real breathing window in this lane.
edits.after: Riftwalk answers Disdain — 475 range, 16s at rank 1, and it shields him as he charges. Blink the instant he commits, before Purge locks onto you, and reset; your one breathing window.

edits.before: Fear Beyond Death executes you below the HP threshold and fears on the kill — if you Riftwalk toward him while low, he yanks you with E and the execute lands, so never blink into R range.
edits.after: Fear Beyond Death is 100s at rank 1 and reaches 2500 units, impaling the FIRST champion in its path and executing below the threshold — never blink in low, and put a body in the line.

edits.before: Land E Disdain to flip you in, then channel W Purge to chunk you with physical percent-HP before you can blink away
edits.after: Land Disdain to flip you in, then Purge — it auto-prioritises whoever he has just struck with another ability

edits.before: Survive to 6, then use Riftwalk to dodge his E Disdain flip and disengage before W Purge grinds you down
edits.after: Survive to 6, then blink out of Disdain on the commit — Purge slows Urgot while it runs, so that is your exit

edits.after: - Urgot Disdain: 16s at rank 1 and only 475 range — sidestep it and he has no way to start, but it shields him as he charges. - Q shield spent on poke is a death you scheduled. - Hold the R for the fight that decides something.

edits.before: Track Urgot’s Disdain (Flip): His flip engage — sidestep it and he has no way to start. The whole green-light system is its cooldown.
edits.after: Disdain: 16s at rank 1, 475 range, it shields him, and it stops on the first champion. Purge then locks onto whoever he last hit.

edits.after: His flip engage: 475 range, 16s at rank 1, and it shields him. Sidestep it and he has no way to start.

edits.before: Stacked Riftwalk Kassadin is the endgame boss: blink onto carries, Q-silence the counterplay, and leave before the fight even registers you.
edits.after: Stacked Riftwalk Kassadin is the endgame boss: blink onto carries, Null Sphere to interrupt a channel, and leave before the fight registers you.

notes: I did NOT touch the repeated claim that Urgot's Echoing Flames passive and autos deal percent-max-HP damage — it appears in early, late, whys[0], whys[3], whys[6], spikes[0], spikes[3] and wants.foe[0], and it drives the concrete instruction 'Rod of Ages HP just feeds it'. Riot's description says only 'dealing physical damage', and Urgot carries no percentHealth flag anywhere in his kit file even though the builder tracks that flag on other champions. That makes it unverified rather than wrong, and if it IS wrong the anti-HP itemisation advice is backwards, so it needs a human decision rather than a guess from me. Logged in unverified. Separately: the page writes his E as 'Disdain (Flip)'; the Riot name is just Disdain, and I dropped the parenthetical only in the strings I rewrote so the two forms will coexist until someone normalises it.
